decisions.reason: The candidate already has a message-176 introduction covering food-safe materials and FOOD_SERVICE scope; expanding service-access scope adds no further material requirement change.

The candidate's message-176 MODIFY already captures sanitation access, liquid-trap prevention, and FOOD_SERVICE scope. General component servicing access does not require another dispensing-path change.
Food-service maintenance access does not alter the unit's structural rigidity or vibration-control behavior.
The candidate already has a message-176 scope change adding FOOD_SERVICE based on the explicit liquid-separation clause; service accessibility adds no further isolation semantics.
The candidate's message-176 MODIFY already applies removable-whisk behavior to retail food service. The general component-service-access change does not necessarily add another whisk attribute.
Considering food-service maintenance access does not change the milestone-local strategy of using off-the-shelf prototype electronics.
The source decision concerns access for servicing internal components, not the accepted enclosure size or form factor.

The candidate already has a message-176 update requiring CAD-file retention. The service-access scope change does not necessarily modify the CAD deliverable beyond that independently stated documentation requirement.
Maintenance access for replaceable components does not alter the spout's geometry, orientation, material, appearance, or pour direction.
The source does not change component selections, compatibility requirements, or the BOM artifact; any future replacement documentation would require a separate concrete decision.
